title: FileDropzone accept option matches by MIME type, not extension
answers: Why does my FileDropzone accept wrong file types (e.g. .txt accepted when only .yml allowed)?
FileDropzone extension filter not working / accepting unwanted files
How to properly restrict FileDropzone to specific file extensions
body:
Symptom: a FileDropzone configured with `accept: ['.yaml', '.yml']` also silently accepts files with unrelated extensions (e.g. a `.txt` file) because its MIME-type detection buckets '.txt' and '.yml' together.
Root cause: Grafana's `FileDropzone` `options.accept` buckets files by inferred MIME type, not by filename extension, so extensions that share a MIME bucket slip through.
Fix pattern: pass a custom `options.validator(file)` that re-checks `file.name.toLowerCase().endsWith(ext)` against the allowed extension list and returns a `{ code: 'file-invalid-type', message }` object when it fails (see `validateYamlFileExtension` in public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/import-to-gma/steps/Step1AlertmanagerResources.tsx).
Constraints: only needed when the accepted extensions map to MIME types shared with extensions you want to reject; pure extension lists that map 1:1 to unique MIME types don't need this.
applies: Any usage of Grafana's FileDropzone component with options.accept restricted by file extension
